scene_text: Dussasana pulls at Draupadi’s robe as endless layers of cloth miraculously appear, piling on the floor while the stunned court watches.
Rama standing on Indra’s radiant chariot, drawing his bow and releasing the blazing Brahmastra toward Ravana.
Krishna revealing his cosmic form to Arjuna, his body filled with countless faces, arms, weapons, and gods, radiating light like a thousand suns.
Krishna reveals his universal form blazing like a thousand suns, with countless faces, arms, and weapons filling the sky while Arjuna bows in awe.
Dussasana drags a disheveled Draupadi by her long dark hair into the royal assembly while the elders sit silent and the Pandavas watch in rage.
Rama releases the Brahma weapon from his drawn bow as Ravana and his chariot erupt in a blazing cosmic fire.
Arjuna sees multitudes of warriors and kings rushing helplessly into Krishna’s flaming mouths like moths flying into fire.
In a silent, shocked hall of kings, Yudhishthira describes Draupadi’s beauty and virtue before staking her, while the elders cry out in dismay.
Bhishma falls from his chariot at sunset, his body held above the ground by countless arrows piercing him.
Wounded Abhimanyu stands amid enemies, lifting a broken chariot wheel above his head like a blazing discus while dust and arrows swirl around him.
Arjuna kneeling in awe before the blazing universal form while the entire universe—stars, gods, and beings—appears within Krishna’s vast body.
Krishna and Arjuna stand in the chariot between the armies as Krishna reveals the final teaching of surrender and devotion.
Dussasana violently dragging Draupadi by the hair into the crowded Kuru royal court while kings and elders sit in stunned silence.
Bhishma falling from his chariot at sunset, his body suspended above the ground by countless arrows forming a bed beneath him while warriors watch in shock.
Dussasana drags the trembling Draupadi by force into the crowded Kuru assembly while kings watch in silence.
Arjuna, overwhelmed with grief, drops his bow and sits down in his chariot between the two massive armies on the battlefield of Kurukshetra.
Within Krishna’s vast body Arjuna beholds the entire universe—gods, sages, serpents, sun and moon—contained in a single cosmic vision.
Young Abhimanyu charges alone into Drona’s radiant circular battle formation, his chariot breaking through ranks of armored warriors.
Six veteran Kaurava warriors surround the lone Abhimanyu as his shattered chariot stands amid fallen soldiers.
Balarama sits beneath a tree in meditation as a vast white thousand‑headed serpent emerges from his mouth and glides toward the ocean while divine serpents gather to receive him.
Balarama sits beneath a tree in meditation as a विशाल white thousand‑headed serpent emerges from his mouth and moves toward the ocean.
Indra’s radiant chariot descending from the sky before Yudhishthira, who refuses to board unless the faithful dog may come with him.
Indra’s radiant chariot descends from the sky while Yudhishthira stands beside a faithful dog, refusing heaven unless the animal may come.
The hunter transforming into Shiva beside Uma, holding the trident and Pinaka bow, as the defeated Arjuna kneels before him.
Warriors and kings rushing helplessly into the flaming mouths of the cosmic deity like moths flying into a fire.
Krishna leaping from Arjuna’s chariot in fury, golden garments streaming as he charges toward Bhishma with the blazing Sudarshana discus in his raised hand.
Abhimanyu, blood‑soaked and roaring, lifts a broken chariot wheel above his head like a discus while surrounded by hostile kings.
At Prabhasa, drunken Yadava warriors tear up blades of eraka grass that transform into glowing iron bolts as they turn on one another in a chaotic twilight battlefield.
The hunter Jara kneels in terror before Krishna, realizing he has shot the yellow‑robed god through the heel as the dying deity shines with celestial light.
Under moonlit waters of the Ganges, Ganga calmly releases a newborn child into the river while Santanu watches in silent anguish.
